item.title: Badagry: The Intersection of History, Culture, and Coastal Heritage
item.description: Badagry’s roots trace back to approximately 1425 A.D. along the coast of the Gberefu peninsula. Before the town’s formal establishment, the coastal inhabitants relied heavily on fishing, farming, and salt making from the ocean. According to native tradition, the town was founded by a renowned farmer named Agbedeh, who lived at Gberefu Sea Beach and maintained farmland across the lagoon.
